markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) SASRec can represent recent transitions and longer dependencies, but its attention does not guarantee that repeated recent interests outweigh incidental older events. This matches the simulator’s reported intent mismatch. (2) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin, motivating stronger candidate discrimination; these training diagnostics do not establish validation performance. (3) Embedding similarity scores near the 0.5 zero-cosine reference provide insufficient evidence for severe collapse. Prioritize ranking and intent experiments before diversity regularization.

**Related work.** (1) MSMT-LSI and HeteroTempRec motivate separating recent intent from persistent preference, without demonstrating gains here. (2) D2MFRec motivates gated interests but warns about sparse-history instability, favoring a small residual over multiple routing modules. (3) gSASRec and scaled cross-entropy motivate stronger sampled objectives; R²NS cautions against introducing hard negatives immediately.

### Framework and directions

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate discrimination | gBCE, sampled CE | Uniform multi-negative CE | False negatives remain possible |
| Current intent | Temporal fusion, gated interests | Recency-and-recurrence residual | Recurrence is an imperfect intent proxy |
| Useful complements | Directed interaction graphs | Smoothed transition residual | Association cannot verify compatibility |

### Candidate assessment

Scores are Originality/Potential/User alignment/Model alignment/Difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

1. **Uniform multi-negative sampled CE: 2/7/4/9/3.** O: + focused adaptation, − established objective. P: + reusable baseline, − limited architectural contribution. U: + discriminates plausible alternatives, − ignores stale intent. M: + targets weak margins, − training separation may not transfer. D: + localized loss change, − negative masking needs care.
2. **Recency-and-recurrence gated SASRec: 4/8/8/8/5.** O: + couples recurrence with recent support, − gating is established. P: + interpretable intent mechanism, − sparse histories weaken evidence. U: + targets stale influence and broad matches, − cannot verify compatibility. M: + sampled CE targets confusion, − gains remain hypothetical. D: + small causal residual, − predictor parity requires testing.
3. **Directed transition residual: 4/7/7/6/5.** O: + directional evidence, − established graph principle. P: + useful complement hypothesis, − sparse transitions. U: + supports next-step usefulness, − associations can still duplicate needs. M: + sharpens alternatives, − popular transitions may dominate. D: + sparse counts, − smoothing and inference add work.

### Selected experiment

At 0% progress, choose **candidate 2**, using candidate 1 as its shared objective baseline. Add a gated pool of recent events, weighted by repeated similarity support, to SASRec. This explicitly targets older incidental influence and broadly related choices crowding out specific recent interests; multi-negative CE targets Electronics’ weak separation.

Ablate loss-only, recency-only, and recurrence gating. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Treat compatibility and satisfied demand as unresolved; no improvement is claimed before evaluation.

idea.description: Recency-and-recurrence gated SASRec with uniform multi-negative sampled cross-entropy. Preserve one independently trained model per category. At every causal prediction position, augment the SASRec representation with a small pool of recent item embeddings weighted by recency and similarity support from preceding events. Learn a scalar gate that controls this residual. The proposal targets two observed user failures: excessive influence from older incidental events and broad relatedness displacing specific recent interests. Its sampled objective targets weak positive-versus-negative separation, especially in Electronics.
idea.motivation: The diagnosis supports testing intent weighting and candidate discrimination before collapse penalties. Electronics has a negative tenth-percentile margin, while the simulator describes insufficient emphasis on repeated recent preferences. These observations motivate the experiment but do not establish its causal explanation or expected HR@10 gain. Compatibility, replacement need, and satisfied demand cannot be inferred reliably from the available histories.
idea.implementation_notes: Proposed implementation, not an executed trial. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS with default 200. Begin with a recent window of 10 and 64 shared uniform negatives per batch; compute losses over valid positions in chunks if needed. Mask padding, the target, and observed training positives from negative denominators. Use strictly prefix-only recurrence and gate inputs. Start the residual gate near zero. Use normalized, detached item embeddings to estimate recurrence; retain gradients through pooled values. Similarity is a preference proxy, not proof of matching purpose. Update the predictor writer with the identical module and checkpoint configuration. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), the actual view.model, and compatibility methods. Measure margins using the deployed scoring path; report unavailable metadata breakdowns as unavailable. Select checkpoints using the pinned validation procedure and report macro HR@10 alongside category values and consumed GPU time. Do not use hidden test data or fabricated metadata.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, initialize SASRec and a small gate using seed 42.
For each training batch and valid position t:
    h_t = SASRec(prefix through t)
    W_t = last min(10, prefix_length) nonpadding positions
    For j in W_t:
        support_j = mean(max(0, cosine(stopgrad(e_j), stopgrad(e_k)))) over k < j
        support_j = 0 if no preceding events
        a_j = -softplus(decay) * (t-j) + softplus(strength) * support_j
    r_t = sum(softmax(a)_j * e_j)
    g_t = sigmoid(MLP([h_t, r_t, log(1+prefix_length)]))
    z_t = LayerNorm(h_t + g_t * r_t)
    Sample 64 uniform negative IDs; mask target and observed training positives.
    loss_t = -log_softmax([score(z_t, target), valid_negative_scores])[0]
    Optimize mean(loss_t) over valid positions.
Evaluate loss-only, recency-only, and full recurrence variants using pinned validation.
Export the selected architecture and identical scoring logic through the predictor writer.

originality.positive: Combines explicit recurrence support with a gated recent residual in a narrowly testable SASRec extension.
originality.negative: Temporal pooling, gating, and multi-negative objectives are established techniques; novelty is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact foundation for studying when repeated recent evidence should alter sequential recommendations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse histories and noisy learned similarity may limit transfer, and the mechanism cannot establish compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small pooling and gating module while retaining SASRec training and category routing.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal recurrence, negative masking, diagnostic adapters, and predictor serialization require careful consistency.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention baseline and item-embedding scoring architecture.
limitations: Attention alone does not guarantee emphasis on repeated recent intent or establish item compatibility.

related_work.title: MSMT-LSI
contributions: The supplied search summary describes temporal embeddings and separate long- and short-term attention networks.
limitations: Reported Amazon Beauty/Games findings do not establish gains on the specified four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: HeteroTempRec
contributions: The supplied summary describes local and global temporal modeling with adaptive fusion.
limitations: Its additional architectural components require separate compute and ablation justification here.

related_work.title: D2MFRec
contributions: Motivates gated single- and multiple-interest representations.
limitations: The supplied summary notes instability from dispersed interests under sparse, irregular behavior.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Addresses negative-sampling overconfidence through calibrated gBCE.
limitations: Calibration does not directly resolve stale interests or unsupported compatibility assumptions.

related_work.title: Scaled cross-entropy
contributions: Motivates evaluating stronger cross-entropy objectives for sequential recommenders.
limitations: Objective improvements elsewhere do not establish gains under the pinned evaluation protocol.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: The supplied summary motivates warm-up before introducing harder negatives.
limitations: Hard-negative curricula introduce tuning and false-negative risks beyond the proposed initial uniform-negative experiment.

related_work.title: Revisiting Graph Projections
contributions: Motivates directed, temporally ordered item relationships as an alternative residual.
limitations: Observed transitions cannot reliably distinguish complements, substitutes, and satisfied needs.
